props.title: Phas Gaye Re Obama
props.initialSlug: Kidnapping comedy during India's recession woes

sections.content: **Phas Gaye Re Obama** (2010) brilliantly satirizes both the 2008 American financial crisis and Indian kidnapping gangs through its clever premise of kidnappers facing their own economic downturn. Director Subhash Kapoor crafts a sharp commentary that parallels **Peepli Live** (2010) in its ability to tackle serious socioeconomic issues through dark humor. The film's protagonist - an NRI businessman who's lost everything in the US recession - becomes an unwitting catalyst for exposing how globalization impacts even rural Indian criminal enterprises.

sections.content: The film stands out for how it weaves together multiple narrative threads examining economic disparity. Like **Rocket Singh: Salesman of the Year** (2009), it uses workplace dynamics and business practices as a lens to explore larger societal issues. Rajat Kapoor's performance as the desperate NRI businessman perfectly captures the anxiety of middle-class aspirations crumbling under economic pressure.

The film's greatest strength lies in how it uses comedy to illuminate serious themes about globalization's reach into rural India. Similar to **Bheja Fry** (2007) and **Mithya** (2008), it employs situational humor and mistaken identities to drive both its plot and social commentary. The kidnappers' struggles with "recession" create genuinely funny moments while highlighting how international economic forces affect even illegal enterprises. sections.content: **Phas Gaye Re Obama** helped pave the way for a new wave of intelligent Hindi comedies that blend social commentary with entertainment. Films like **Hindi Medium** (2017) and **Angrezi Medium** (2020) followed its template of using humor to address serious issues. The film's success demonstrated audiences' appetite for comedies that don't sacrifice substance for laughs.
